proof.text: Put $B_n=(A_n)_Y$ and $K_n=B_n[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](1) with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ (choose an algebraic closure containing this field): $K_n$ is bounded constructible. The coefficient unit is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]: for any complex $C$, multiplication $C\otimes_{B_n}B_n\to C$ has inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, commutes with differentials, and preserves acyclicity. These mutually inverse maps are defined on the presheaf tensors and hence on the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. In particular, for a module sheaf $M[0]$, $K_n\otimes^L_{B_n}M=M[0]$, so its cohomology is zero outside degree zero. This is Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and therefore $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$, with one bound independent of $n$.

proof.text:
Let $q_{n,m}:B_n\to B_m$ be coefficient reduction, $n\geq m\geq1$, and take $t_{n,m}=q_{n,m}$ in degree zero, with the target read by restriction of scalars. These maps have $t_{n,n}=1$ and $t_{n,j}=t_{m,j}t_{n,m}$ because quotient homomorphisms do. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2), the K-flat unit of Step 1 itself computes $K_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m$. Its adjoint normalization map in [def-trf-adic-system] is
$$\nu_{n,m}:B_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m\longrightarrow B_m,\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto q_{n,m}(a)b.$$
The inverse is $b\mapsto1\otimes b$: balancing gives $a\otimes b=1\otimes q_{n,m}(a)b$. Thus this is the canonical isomorphism induced by the chosen transition, not merely an abstract identification of the two objects. For $n\geq m\geq j$, both normalization composites send $(a\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $q_{n,j}(a)q_{m,j}(b)c$, proving the required coherence. No flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$ is asserted or used.

proof.text:
Write $g=g_Y$. At finite level let $d_{g,n}:Lg^*B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n$ be the canonical coefficient-unit identification. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] it is $c_n\circ\lambda_{B_n}$, with $c_n$ exactly the constant-section structure map in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](1). Clause (3) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] gives
$$q_{n,m}c_n=c_m g^{-1}(q_{n,m}).$$
(The clause applies to every coefficient homomorphism, not just adjacent levels.) The comparisons $\lambda$ are natural, so this is also the derived transition square for $d_{g,n}$. By [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk], the canonical identification of a constant stalk with $A_n$ sends $a$ to the germ of the constant section $a$. The defining adjunct for $c_n$ preserves that section. Hence $d_{g,n}$ sends $a$ to $a$ between the source and target constant stalks. This compares stalks at the appropriate pulled-back points; it does not assert that $g$ fixes the geometric point. Together with Step 2 this gives the geometric Weil maps of a normalized system.

proof.text:
Let $\Phi$ be the model Frobenius. By [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] and [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], if $H=F_Y^a$ is absolute $q$-power Frobenius, then $\Phi=g\circ H$: the arithmetic Galois map in the factorization is inverse to $g$. Put $P=LH^*$. The canonical comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], compatible with this factorization, is
$$L\Phi^*\xrightarrow{c}P Lg^*\xrightarrow{\tau_{Lg^*(-)}}Lg^*.$$
Here $\tau:P\to\mathrm{id}$ is precisely the trivialization specified by [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] with exponent $a$. That statement describes it as the adjoint of restriction along the relative-Frobenius isomorphisms of site objects. Restriction along each such isomorphism takes the constant section $b$ to $b$, so its inverse and its adjoint also preserve $b$. Thus at the coefficient unit $\tau$ is the canonical constant-section identification. The constant-ring composition equation of [lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition] now gives
$$d_{g,n}\circ\kappa_{B_n}=d_{H,n}\circ P(d_{g,n})\circ c_{B_n}=d_{\Phi,n}.$$
In the first equality use naturality of $\tau$ at $d_{g,n}$ and its just-computed unit value. The derived maps here are the ordinary constant-coefficient maps in degree zero: [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] identifies module pullback with exact inverse image for every scheme map. All hypotheses hold: $Y$ is in characteristic $p$, $a\geq1$, and $A_n$ is finite and killed by $\ell^n$ prime to $p$.

proof.text: Take the model Weil map to be $d_{\Phi,n}$. It is an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and Step 4 identifies it with $d_{g,n}\kappa_{B_n}$. Thus it is the canonical model map, with the same underlying $K_n$, in [sk-d-weil]. Its transition square commutes: on a constant local coefficient $a\in A_n$ both $q_{n,m}d_{\Phi,n}$ and $d_{\Phi,m}L\Phi^*(q_{n,m})$ send its pulled-back germ to $q_{n,m}(a)$. Constant sections locally generate the constant sheaves, so equality there proves equality of the sheaf maps; [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] computes these derived pullbacks termwise. The same calculation shows that its map on constant stalks is $a\mapsto a$, using the identifications of [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk]. For the derived normalizations of Step 2, either path around the Frobenius square sends a local tensor $a\otimes b$ to $q_{n,m}(a)b$. Hence the model and geometric maps both commute with the canonical reductions as well as with the transitions. This proves every finite-level Weil-compatibility requirement of [def-trf-adic-system].

proof.text: Put $R=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,Y}=\varprojlim_nB_n$. By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2), $R[0]$ is derived complete and its canonical reductions are $B_n[0]$. In the reduction-tower construction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] one may take the K-flat unit complex $P=R[0]$ itself: multiplication identifies $R\otimes_RB_n$ with $B_n$, takes $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ to the limit projection $\pi_n$, and takes $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$ to coefficient reduction. Thus this reduction tower is exactly the tower of Step 2, including all transition maps. Derived completeness in [def-weil-derived-complete] says that $R[0]$ is an integral realization of this tower in the Roos-triangle sense required by [def-trf-adic-system]. The integral canonical map of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](2)–(3) has components $c_n g^{-1}(\pi_n)$; by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-reduction-tower], its canonical quotient and transition identifications are precisely those of Step 3. Hence it is the integral lift of that compatible geometric datum. Finally [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](4) defines $E_Y$ and its canonical Weil map as the rationalizations of this $R[0]$ and its map. The constructed integral model therefore rationalizes to the prescribed constant $E$-Weil sheaf. This rationalizes the completed integral realization, not an individual torsion ring $A_n$.

title: Compatible constant Weil datum
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and $E=\Q_\ell$ with coefficient rings $A_n=\Z_\ell/\ell^n$, $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. The constant $E$-Weil sheaf with its canonical structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] admits a normalized compatible integral model in the sense of [def-trf-adic-system]: at level $n$ it is the constant coefficient sheaf $(A_n)_Y$ in degree zero, and its canonical derived reduction to level $m$, $1\leq m\leq n$, is $(A_m)_Y$ in degree zero. The transition maps are the coefficient reductions. For each level, the canonical model-Frobenius Weil map of [sk-d-weil] and the geometric-Frobenius Weil map commute with the transitions and induce the identity on the constant stalks under their canonical identifications with $A_n$. Its rationalized $E$-stage is the constant object $E_Y$. Under the canonical scheme/Galois Frobenius comparison $\kappa:L\Phi^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_Y^*$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], the model map is the composite of $\kappa$ with the geometric map.
